intro:
José Mourinho has told a new documentary that he agreed to replace Sir Alex Ferguson as Manchester United manager, a development revealed by BBC Sport. The programme sheds fresh light on the succession process that followed Ferguson's departure from Old Trafford.

David Moyes ultimately took over the job in 2013. BBC Sport's reporting highlights how close Manchester United's post‑Ferguson era came to unfolding differently, according to Mourinho's account in the film.

sections.heading: What Mourinho said in the documentary
sections.text:
According to BBC Sport, Mourinho has disclosed in a recent documentary that he agreed to take over from Sir Alex Ferguson at Manchester United. The report places Mourinho's revelation alongside the well‑known fact that David Moyes succeeded Ferguson in 2013. Beyond that central claim, the documentary appears aimed at revisiting a pivotal moment in United's modern history.

The documentary format has become a common way for high‑profile managers and players to offer retrospective insights. In this instance, Mourinho's contribution — as reported by BBC Sport — adds a new layer to the narrative about United's managerial transition after one of the game's most influential tenures.

sections.heading: Context: Ferguson's exit and Moyes's appointment
sections.text:
Sir Alex Ferguson's decision to step down marked the end of a prolonged and trophy‑filled era for Manchester United. His retirement in 2013 prompted a high‑stakes search for his successor and generated intense public and media interest in who would inherit the role at Old Trafford.

David Moyes was appointed to succeed Ferguson in 2013. Moyes, who had built a reputation managing at a stable Premier League club prior to the United appointment, became the man entrusted with navigating the club through a period of transition after Ferguson's long reign. The contrast between Ferguson's era and the subsequent years has been a frequent subject of analysis in football circles.

analysis:
If Mourinho's account in the documentary is accepted at face value, it reframes part of the story surrounding Manchester United's post‑Ferguson succession. Football clubs of United's size often explore multiple avenues when replacing an iconic manager, and retrospective admissions like this can illuminate behind‑the‑scenes dynamics that were not public at the time. Analysts might see Mourinho's revelation as part of a broader trend of high‑profile figures revisiting defining career moments through documentaries.

That said, the only verified sequence of events in the public record remains that Sir Alex Ferguson left Manchester United in 2013 and David Moyes took over that year. Mourinho's reported claim, as presented by BBC Sport, adds an intriguing what‑if to the narrative rather than altering the documented outcome.

faq.question: Did José Mourinho replace Sir Alex Ferguson as Manchester United manager?
faq.answer: No. BBC Sport reports that while Mourinho has said in a documentary he agreed to replace Sir Alex Ferguson, the managerial appointment ultimately went to David Moyes, who succeeded Ferguson in 2013.

faq.question: When did David Moyes become Manchester United manager?
faq.answer: David Moyes succeeded Sir Alex Ferguson as Manchester United manager in 2013, following Ferguson's departure.

faq.question: Where did this information about Mourinho come from?
faq.answer: The detail about Mourinho saying he agreed to replace Ferguson was revealed in a new documentary and reported by BBC Sport.

conclusion: BBC Sport's report that José Mourinho has claimed in a documentary he agreed to take over from Sir Alex Ferguson offers a striking retrospective angle on Manchester United's 2013 managerial succession. While David Moyes remains the documented successor, Mourinho's revelation contributes another footnote to one of the most discussed transitions in modern British football.
